title: Bedmi Puri with Aloo Sabzi
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Wheat flour + urad dal paste for bedmi

recipe: Prepare a stiff dough with wheat flour mixed with spiced urad dal paste. Roll into thick puris and deep-fry till crisp and golden.
Make a spiced potato-tomato sabzi.
Serve hot bedmi puris with the aloo sabzi, often accompanied by pickle or chutney.
tips: Classic UP/Delhi-border breakfast – the urad dal gives the puri its distinctive texture and flavour.
Best eaten fresh and hot.

title: Kachori with Dal Filling & Aloo Sabzi
jainNotes: Contains onion and potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Spiced dal filling (urad or moong dal)

recipe: Stuff spiced dal mixture into wheat dough, seal and deep-fry into crisp kachoris.
Prepare a simple or spicy potato sabzi.
Serve hot kachoris with sabzi – a popular street and home breakfast across UP.
tips: Iconic UP breakfast, especially in cities like Lucknow, Kanpur and Varanasi.
Dal-stuffed versions are most traditional.

title: Kachori with Pea Filling & Aloo Sabzi
jainNotes: Contains onion and potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Stuff spiced pea mixture into wheat dough, seal and deep-fry into crisp kachoris.
Prepare a simple or spicy potato sabzi.
Serve hot kachoris with sabzi – a popular street and home breakfast across UP.
tips: Iconic UP breakfast with pea-stuffed kachoris.
A popular winter variant when fresh peas are abundant.

title: Puri Aloo
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Knead a stiff dough, roll and deep-fry puris till puffed and golden.
Prepare a spiced potato curry (often with tomato and mild spices).
Serve hot puris with aloo sabzi – everyday and festive breakfast favourite.
tips: Simple, satisfying and ubiquitous across Uttar Pradesh.
Often paired with jalebi or a sweet on special mornings.

title: Awadhi Mutton Biryani
jainNotes: Contains mutton and onion - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Yogurt, fried onions, saffron, kewra, whole spices, ghee

recipe: Marinate mutton with yogurt, spices and fried onions. Partially cook the rice.
Layer meat and rice in a heavy pot, add saffron milk, kewra and ghee. Seal and cook on dum.
Serve with raita and salan.
tips: Refined Lucknowi/Awadhi classic – fragrant, lightly spiced and elegant.
Dum cooking is essential for authentic flavour.

title: Tehri
jainNotes: Contains onion and potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Turmeric, whole spices, mustard oil or ghee, salt

recipe: Fry sliced onion and whole spices in mustard oil or ghee. Add vegetables and turmeric.
Add rinsed rice and water. Cook covered till the rice and vegetables are done.
Serve hot with raita or plain yogurt – a comforting one-pot meal.
tips: Classic vegetarian rice dish of UP – yellow from turmeric and full of seasonal vegetables.
Especially popular on Sundays and for light meals.

title: Galouti Kebab
jainNotes: Contains mutton and onion - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Papaya paste, aromatic spices, fried onion, ghee

recipe: Mince the meat extremely fine and marinate with raw papaya (for tenderness), spices and fried onion.
Shape into small patties and shallow-fry gently in ghee on a low flame till cooked through.
Serve with ulte tawa paratha or roomali roti and chutney.
tips: Legendary Lucknowi kebab – so soft it melts in the mouth.
Traditionally made for a toothless Nawab; texture is everything.

title: Nihari (Mutton Shank)
jainNotes: Contains mutton and onion - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Whole spices, wheat flour for thickening, ghee, ginger, onion

recipe: Slow-cook mutton shank with whole spices, onion and water for several hours until the meat is falling off the bone and the gravy is rich.
Thicken slightly with a wheat-flour slurry if needed. Finish with ginger juliennes and ghee.
Serve with sheermal, kulcha or naan – traditionally a winter breakfast or hearty dinner.
tips: Awadhi slow-cooked stew made with mutton shank – deep, aromatic and comforting.
Long, gentle cooking is non-negotiable.

title: Nihari (Mutton with Bones)
jainNotes: Contains mutton and onion - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Whole spices, wheat flour for thickening, ghee, ginger, onion

recipe: Slow-cook mutton with whole spices, onion and water for several hours until the meat is falling off the bone and the gravy is rich.
Thicken slightly with a wheat-flour slurry if needed. Finish with ginger juliennes and ghee.
Serve with sheermal, kulcha or naan – traditionally a winter breakfast or hearty dinner.
tips: Awadhi slow-cooked stew with bone-in mutton – deep, aromatic and comforting.
Long, gentle cooking is non-negotiable.

title: Shahi Paneer
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.

ingredients.name: Onion, tomato, cashew-almond paste, cream, spices

recipe: Prepare a rich gravy with fried onion, tomato, cashew-almond paste and aromatic spices.
Add paneer cubes and finish with cream, a touch of saffron or kewra.
Serve with naan, roti or jeera rice.
tips: Rich, mildly sweet Awadhi-style paneer curry popular across UP.
The nut paste gives the characteristic silky texture.

title: Samosa
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Prepare a stiff dough and a spiced potato-pea filling.
Shape into triangular samosas, seal well and deep-fry on medium heat till golden and crisp.
Serve with tamarind and green chutney – the classic UP street snack.
tips: UP is widely regarded as the home of the perfect samosa.
Crisp outer shell and well-spiced filling are essential.

title: Aloo Tikki Chaat
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) and onion - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Yogurt, chutneys, sev, onion for chaat

recipe: Mash spiced potatoes, shape into tikkis and shallow-fry or pan-fry till crisp.
Top with beaten yogurt, sweet and green chutneys, chopped onion, sev and chaat masala.
Serve immediately as a popular street chaat.
tips: Chaat originated in Uttar Pradesh and remains a defining street-food tradition.
Balance of sweet, sour, spicy and crunchy is key.

title: Nimona
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) and onion - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Coarsely grind green peas. Sauté onion, spices and tomato, then add the pea paste and potato.
Cook into a thick, flavourful gravy.
Serve with rice or roti – a classic winter dish of eastern UP and Awadh.
tips: Homestyle green-pea curry unique to the region.
Fresh winter peas give the best flavour.

title: Baati Chokha
jainNotes: Contains onion and potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Brinjal, tomato, potato, onion for chokha
Mustard oil, green chilli for chokha

recipe: Knead a stiff dough with wheat flour, ghee and salt. Shape into hard balls and bake or roast till cooked through and hard.
Break open, pour ghee inside. Serve with smoky mashed chokha of roasted brinjal, tomato and potato with onion.
A rustic Bundelkhandi speciality.
tips: Hard-baked wheat balls with generous ghee and smoky chokha – from the Bundelkhand region of UP.
Similar in spirit to Bihari litti but distinct.
